design.changes: A normal patch changes only its code slot, document slot, directory entry and corresponding unwind entries. A relocation also changes its jump gate, allocator record and exception-directory length.
design.data: Legacy globals keep their RVAs; new combat functions accept an explicit 1152-byte context pointer.
design.entrypoints: Existing function entry RVAs stay stable. An oversized replacement can use a five-byte relative jump gate to a reserved .mods implementation slot.
design.integrity: Per-module SHA-256 for used code and JSON; ABI digest for declared public contract. Hashes detect stale/corrupt patches, not malicious executable semantics.
design.metadata: Read-only .llm section with a 512-byte header, 128 fixed 192-byte directory entries and individually reserved UTF-8 JSON document slots.
design.runtime: Handwritten x64 instruction bytes plus Windows system DLL imports; no compiler, assembler, downloaded static library or language runtime.

limits: The verifier validates layout, addresses, hashes, padding and supported unwind profiles; it cannot prove raw instructions satisfy their prose contract.
A data-layout or import change is a layout migration, not a routine function patch.
Live hot patching and running-process memory writes are not supported.
